title: Mercury Grand Marquis Engines (1975–2011)
description: Every factory engine in the Mercury Grand Marquis by year, 1975–2011: the 460, 400 and 351M V8s, the 255, 302 and 351 Windsors, and the 4.6 SOHC Modular V8.
intro: The Grand Marquis began as the top Mercury Marquis in 1975 and became its own model for 1983. It shared Ford's Panther platform with the Crown Victoria from 1979 until production ended in 2011.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: 1975–1978 Marquis Grand Marquis
intro: The 460 and 400 big-car V8s and, for 1978, the 351M.

generations.name: 1979–1991 (Panther)
intro: The 302 and 351 Windsor V8s and, in 1981–1982 two-doors, the 255; fuel injection from 1983.
The 4.6 SOHC Modular V8, with a dual-exhaust version.
The 4.6 Modular V8 in single- and dual-exhaust (Handling Package and LSE) form; flex-fuel in the last years.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
